chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Fadl ibn Yunus, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), I said: 'When a woman sees purity before sunset, what should she do regarding the prayer?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If she sees purity after four steps of the shadow have passed from the decline of the sun, she should not pray except Asr, because the time for Dhuhr entered upon her while she was in blood, and the time exited from her while she was in blood, so it did not become obligatory upon her to pray Dhuhr, and what Allah has dropped from her regarding the prayer while she was in blood is more.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'And when the woman sees blood after four steps of the shadow have passed from the decline of the sun, let her refrain from the prayer. So when she becomes clean from the blood, let her make up the Dhuhr prayer, because the time of Dhuhr entered upon her while she was pure, and the time of Dhuhr exited from her while she was pure, so she missed the Dhuhr prayer, therefore making it up became obligatory upon her.'

key_terms.أَرْبَعَةُ أَقْدَامٍ: Four steps (a measure of shadow length indicating time passage)
key_terms.زَوَالِ الشَّمْس: Decline of the sun (start of Dhuhr time)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for making up Dhuhr prayer if a woman's menstruation starts or ends near sunset?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between missed (qada) and exempted (mu'af) prayers based on the precise moment of purity or impurity relative to the solar shadow's movement. It establishes that if a woman becomes pure after the Dhuhr time window has closed due to the shadow's decline, she is exempt from Dhuhr and only prays Asr; conversely, if she becomes impure after Dhuhr time has entered while pure, she must make up Dhuhr upon cleansing. This ruling underscores the Shia principle that the validity of a prayer depends on the state of the worshipper at the specific boundaries of its prescribed time.
